title: Brewers vs. Dodgers NLCS Game 4 FAQ: Time, Channel, Streaming & Key Details (8 ET)
body:
Milwaukee will be just one win away from ending a 44‑year championship drought when it takes the field for Game 4 of the National League Championship Series on Thursday night. The Brewers, who have surged to a commanding 3‑0 series lead over the Los Angeles Dodgers, are poised to force a decisive Game 5 that could send the Brew Crew to the World Series for the first time since 1982. A victory would not only break the longest postseason gap in franchise history but also cement Milwaukee’s resurgence under manager Craig Counsell, whose steady hand has guided the team through a season defined by clutch hitting, dominant pitching and a revitalized clubhouse culture.

The Brewers have earned their advantage by combining a potent offense with a deep rotation that has consistently stifled opponents. Right‑hander Brandon Woodruff, who posted a sub‑2.00 ERA in the regular season, is slated to start the pivotal Game 4, and his ability to locate pitches on the edges of the strike zone will be crucial against a Dodgers lineup that has struggled to string together hits in the series. Meanwhile, the middle of the Milwaukee order—Christian Yelich, William Contreras and rookie sensation Freddy Peralta—has delivered timely runs, turning close contests into comfortable leads. Their collective batting average of .312 in the series underscores a balanced attack that can manufacture runs against any pitcher, a trait the Dodgers will need to neutralize if they hope to stave off elimination.

Los Angeles, meanwhile, finds itself on the brink of a historic collapse. The Dodgers entered the series as the defending champions and carried the weight of a franchise accustomed to deep postseason runs. Yet, after dropping the first three games, the pressure to perform has intensified dramatically. Starting pitcher Tyler Anderson, who has struggled with command in recent outings, will take the mound for the Dodgers, tasked with keeping the Brewers’ potent lineup at bay while his own offense attempts to spark a comeback. The Dodgers’ bullpen, a hallmark of their success in previous years, will also be under scrutiny; any misstep could hand Milwaukee the decisive run that ends the series.

Beyond the immediate tactical considerations, the matchup highlights a broader narrative in baseball: the resurgence of mid‑market teams challenging traditional powerhouses. Milwaukee’s rise this season has been fueled by shrewd front‑office moves, including the acquisition of veteran left‑hander Trevor Miller and the promotion of home‑grown talent from its farm system. The Brewers have cultivated a roster that blends experience with youthful vigor, a formula that has resonated with a fan base eager for a return to glory. In contrast, the Dodgers, despite a payroll that consistently ranks among the league’s highest, have faced injuries and inconsistencies that have exposed vulnerabilities in an otherwise formidable squad.

If the Brewers clinch the series in Game 4, they will not only rewrite the narrative of a franchise that has lingered in the shadows of its own history but also set the stage for a World Series that could feature a fresh contender against a team still seeking to cement its modern dynasty. Conversely, a Dodgers victory would extend the series, offering Los Angeles a chance to reassert its dominance and perhaps rewrite the script of a comeback that has become a hallmark of the club’s identity. Either outcome promises to deliver high‑stakes drama for baseball fans worldwide.

As the night approaches, both teams will lean on their strengths while confronting the pressure that only a championship series can generate. Milwaukee’s fans, many of whom have waited four decades for a glimpse of World Series action, will be watching with hopeful anticipation. The Dodgers, determined to avoid a rare early‑round exit, will be fighting to stay alive. Regardless of the result, Game 4 will be a defining moment in a series that has already captured the imagination of the sport, and it will set the tone for whatever lies ahead in the quest for baseball’s ultimate prize.
